answers.answer: Build the 10-card deck top to bottom from 1 randomly dealt Conflict I card (from its shuffled tier), then 5 randomly dealt Conflict II cards, then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘1 card ... Conflict I; 5 cards ... Conflict II; all 4 Conflict III’; ‘Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In either player count, each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and the third Agent (Swordmaster) set aside by the board; 3 troops in their garrison and 9 in supply (12 total troops); 1 water; one cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction Influence tracks; and 0 VP in three-player play versus 1 VP in four-player play.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 5–8: ‘2 Agents’; third Agent set next to board; 12 troops with 3 in garrison; ‘1 water’; Influence cubes on bottom spaces; Score track is 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take your Reveal turn while Agents remain. After you have Revealed, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue cards may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns; after Revealing there is no later turn of yours in the phase on which to play one.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Agent turns are optional; ‘Once you have taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Plot cards can be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and use one matching Agent icon to send exactly one Agent to a space with that icon. The space must be unoccupied. Pay its costs and meet its requirements immediately, before resolving the space or played-card effects; if you cannot pay, you cannot go there. A card with no Agent icon cannot be used for an Agent turn, and one card cannot send multiple Agents.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: ‘play one card’; choose only one matching Agent icon; one card cannot send multiple Agents; space must be unoccupied; costs are paid immediately before effects.

answers.answer: No. You must pay Conspire’s 4-spice entry cost before resolving any effect of the played card, so the card’s spice gain cannot cover a shortfall when you have only 3 spice. Once the cost is paid and the Agent is placed, resolve the board-space effect, card Agent box, and one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: costs are paid before resolving any space or played-card effects; the board space, Agent box, and Faction advancement can then be gained ‘in any order.’ Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: The maximum is 5 troops: all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 additional troops from your garrison, even though 4 are there. Any recruited troops not deployed go to your garrison. Rally Troops normally cannot deploy its recruits because it is not a Combat space, so its 4 recruits go to your garrison.
answers.evidence: Deploy at a Combat space: any or all troops recruited this turn ‘plus up to two more troops from your garrison’; undeployed recruits go to garrison. Rally Troops is ‘not a Combat space, so they go to your garrison.’

answers.answer: The steps are: (1) reveal all cards still in hand, separately from Agent-turn cards; (2) resolve Reveal boxes of the just-revealed cards, in any order; (3) set Combat strength; (4) Clean Up. Reveal boxes on cards played during Agent turns are not used. During Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn steps 1–4; step 2 excludes cards played on Agent turns; step 4 puts all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns in your discard pile.

answers.answer: Yes, the Imperium Row refills immediately, so you may buy a replacement if you can afford it. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card or split one source across cards. Unspent Persuasion is lost at the end of the Reveal turn. An acquired card goes to your discard pile and is not used immediately. Its Acquire effect resolves once at the moment you acquire it.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: Row is refilled immediately; Persuasion may be pooled or split; it cannot be saved; acquired cards go to discard and are not used right away; Acquire box applies at acquisition.

answers.answer: With 3 troops and 4 revealed swords, strength is 10 (3×2 + 4). If your last troop is removed, your strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased by any means, including swords. For strength over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Each Conflict troop is worth 2; each revealed sword 1; without a troop strength is 0 and cannot be increased; over 20 flip to +20 and start at track beginning.

answers.answer: Starting with the First Player and going clockwise, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Passing earlier does not bind later turns; resolve combat after all players involved pass consecutively. ‘When you win’ cards are played only after you have won, before the next phase. If such an Intrigue is drawn as a victory reward, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: First Player clockwise; players with a troop may play any number or pass; no binding pass; consecutive passes resolve combat. Win-trigger cards are after winning; a win-trigger drawn as reward may be played immediately.

answers.answer: A and B tie for first, so neither wins and each takes the second reward. C and D then compete for third; since this is a four-player game, C (the higher of them) takes the third reward and D gets nothing. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, including in two- and three-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. A player with 0 strength gets no reward. After rewards, troops go to their owners’ supply, not their garrisons.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: first-place tie means no winner and tied players get second reward; in a four-player game the other two compete for third. Second-place tie gets third reward; third-place tie nothing; 0 strength no reward; troops return to supply.

answers.answer: During an Agent turn at a Maker space, the space’s normal harvest and any accumulated bonus spice are gained as part of the space effect. During Phase 4: Makers, check The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin; add 1 bonus spice to each space with no Agent. If an Agent moved away and the space is empty by Makers, it receives the bonus spice then.
answers.evidence: Space effects list normal spice at Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, and Great Flat ‘plus any bonus spice’; Makers checks those three and adds 1 if no Agent; ruling says spice accumulates if Agent moves away and space is empty in Phase 4.

answers.answer: The game ends at the end of the round (Recall phase) if any player has 10 or more VP or the Conflict Deck is empty; reaching 10 mid-round does not end it immediately. The players first resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then most VP wins. Tiebreak order is spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Game-end trigger is ‘at the end of a round’; Endgame Intrigue resolves first; listed tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, most recent Reveal turn.

answers.answer: The VP gained at 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you return to 2. The bonus gained at 4 is kept after dropping below 4 and can be earned again by dropping back and advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP; a player must rise above the holder to take it, because merely tying does not transfer it.
answers.evidence: Influence rules: 2 VP is lost below 2 and regained at 2; 4 Influence bonus is not returned and can be earned again; Alliance first at 4, transfers if someone rises higher; merely tying does not take it.

answers.answer: When you lose 1 Influence from 5 while tied there with two opponents, you no longer hold the top position, and one of the previously tied opponents takes the Alliance; since several were tied, you choose which one. If instead you are the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the Alliance; with no other player at 4 or higher to take it, it returns to the board, and you lose its VP.
answers.evidence: If the holder loses Influence while previously tied, a previously tied player takes the Alliance; if several were tied, holder chooses one. Falling to 3 or less loses it; if no one else is at 4+, return it to board.

answers.answer: Discarding means taking a card from your hand unless otherwise specified and putting it in your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from hand, discard pile, or in play to the box; a Reserve card instead returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle early just to inspect the top of an empty deck; reshuffle only when unable to draw.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards section defines discard and trash destinations and eligible locations, including Reserve return; trash is optional except costs/self-trash. Deck exhaustion: reshuffle when unable to draw; cannot reshuffle early to look at top card.

answers.answer: While you control Arrakeen or Carthag, you gain 1 Solari whenever any player sends an Agent there; Imperial Basin control gives you 1 spice on any player’s visit. Winning a Conflict that rewards control of one of those spaces lets you place your Control marker on its flag, replacing an opponent’s marker. If a Conflict for a space you already control is revealed, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control rule: winning places marker, replacing opponent; controller receives the stated bonus whenever any player sends an Agent there; matching Conflict revealed grants optional deployment of one supply troop.

answers.answer: In two-player setup, choose an unused color; put one cube on the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks and all remaining cubes in its supply, with no troops in its garrison. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P, shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards, and place that deck and its three Agents near the supply; use no Rival Leader or solo difficulty rules. After each First Player Agent turn, Hagal takes an Agent turn if it has an Agent in supply; it does not act after the other human’s turns or after a Reveal turn. It has at most three such turns with a Swordmaster First Player, otherwise two, never Reveals, and recalls Agents to supply next round. It does not collect resources, build a deck, score VP, or earn Conflict rewards; it can hold Alliances but cannot claim Control.
answers.evidence: Two-player House Hagal setup and Agent turns; Hagal ‘does not collect resources, build an Imperium deck, earn Conflict rewards or score VP’; can hold Faction Alliances, cannot claim Control; never takes a Reveal turn.

answers.answer: Reveal cards until finding an eligible unoccupied space; if a card’s applicable option is occupied, draw a new card and never switch to its other option. Reshuffle immediately if the deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, then continue revealing. Ignore normal space costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the Hagal card’s icons and instructions. Its troop icons recruit from supply: deploy recruits if the space is Combat, otherwise put them in its garrison. On a Combat space it must also deploy up to two additional garrison troops if available. Harvest Spice follows its card instruction, and any bonus spice taken from a space is removed and returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Hagal Agent-turn rules: occupied option means draw new card, never switch; reshuffle on empty deck or Reshuffle card; ignore space costs/requirements/effects; recruit/deploy troops as described; harvested bonus spice returns to bank.

answers.answer: At Combat start, if Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, reveal a Hagal card in turn order; if it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Add the revealed card’s sword icons to 2 strength per deployed troop. Humans may then play Combat Intrigue before resolution. Hagal gets no reward, but occupies its rank when human rewards are assigned; if it wins a space controlled by a human, remove that human’s Control marker and Hagal does not replace it. A human tie for second pays the third reward to each tied human, even in a two-player game; ordinary third place pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Hagal Combat strength procedure: Reshuffle is redrawn, add sword icons to 2 per troop, then humans may play Combat Intrigue. Hagal gets no rank reward but occupies it; winning removes human Control. Second-place tie pays third reward; ordinary third place pays nothing.
